samples.summary: `sheets import` silently ignores `--start` for exported `ref,value,formula` CSVs, but the agent-facing schema still advertises it unconditionally
samples.evidence: `sheets-import.ts` now branches on `isCellTable(rows)` and calls `buildCellMapFromTable(rows)`, which imports by reference and never uses `parseStartRef(localOpts.start)`. The schema registry entry for `sheets.import` (registry.ts:556-562) still lists `'--start': { type: 'string', ..., description: 'Top-left cell', default: 'A1' }` with no note that it is inert for the header this repo's own `sheets export` writes, and `packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:348` likewise documents `--start <ref> | Top-left cell for import | A1` unqualified (the by-reference behaviour is only mentioned in the *export* section at line 392). `docs/design/cli.md` says the schema is the agent interface; round 8 of this PR treated exactly this class of gap (`--raw` missing from the registry) as blocking and added a flag-name parity test — which cannot catch a flag whose documented meaning no longer matches. Design-fit corollary: the round-trip is opted into explicitly on export (`--raw`) but switched implicitly on import via header sniffing, so a user-authored grid CSV whose first three columns happen to be named ref/value/formula changes import semantics and drops `--start` with no diagnostic.

samples.summary: The design doc's command tree for `sheets export` omits the new `--raw` flag
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:366-367 lists `export <doc-id> <file>` with `[--tab <tab-id>] [--range A1:C10] [--file-format csv|json]` only; `--raw` was added to the command (sheets-export.ts) and is discussed in §8.1 prose (cli.md:923) and in the registry, but the canonical flag listing in the same doc was not updated. Nothing mechanical checks flag parity against design docs.

samples.summary: Published user docs for `wafflebase login` were not updated for the new mandatory confirmation click and the 30s→3min timeout
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:17-31 still says only "The CLI opens your browser for GitHub authentication". The flow now interposes a backend confirmation page the user must click Continue on (CliLoginConfirmMiddleware) and the loopback wait changed from 30s to 3 minutes; both are documented in docs/design/cli.md and rest-api.md but not on the published page users read. This PR did update other published pages (sheets export/import), so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate.

samples.summary: frontend.md not updated for the new `/login?error=<code>` contract the backend now redirects to
samples.evidence: The backend callback now returns browsers to `FRONTEND_URL/login?error=oauth_state` and the login page renders a message keyed off that code (login-form.tsx LOGIN_ERRORS). backend.md and rest-api.md were updated; docs/design/frontend.md's auth lifecycle section (lines 21, 57, 411-415) still describes `/login` only as a redirect target with no error-code contract, so the frontend-side half of a cross-package contract is undocumented in the frontend's canonical doc.

samples.summary: Backend now hand-renders a styled HTML page inline — the only such page in the backend — duplicating brand styling outside the frontend/design system
samples.evidence: `renderConfirmPage` embeds a full HTML document with its own `<style>` block (fonts, card, button colours) in packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts. Grepping `DOCTYPE html` in packages/backend/src returns only this file, so it is the first server-rendered UI in a service the design docs otherwise describe as a JSON API with the SPA on a separate origin. An alternative that fits the existing layering is redirecting to a frontend consent route (the frontend already owns `/login` and the wb-* primitives per design-system-unification.md). Approach/layering preference, not a correctness claim — the choice is at least disclosed in backend.md and rest-api.md.

samples.summary: New `timingSafeEqualStr` helper duplicates an existing constant-time comparison in the backend and is not reused by it
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts:59 already does the same length-check + `timingSafeEqual` inline (`if (a.length !== b.length || !timingSafeEqual(a, b))`). The new shared helper in oauth-state.ts:121 is used by the two new auth call sites but the pre-existing one was left duplicated, so the repo now has two implementations of the same primitive in one package. (The CLI's `nonceMatches` in login.ts is a third, but crossing the backend/CLI package boundary is defensible.)

samples.evidence: Issue #635 (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md) asks only for `status`/`ctx list` to route through `output()` plus `parseOutputFormat`. The diff additionally adds packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts, cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts, a CLI loopback nonce, CSV formula neutralization, `sheets export --raw` + by-reference import, and a frontend login error banner. I record it because it is squarely in this lane, but note the todo file documents these as this panel's own round-2/round-6 requests and rebuts the finding in rounds 5, 6, 8 and 9 — so it is *requested* scope, not unrequested, which is why I am not filing it as major.

samples.summary: `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` is copy-pasted into ~25 action bodies rather than resolved once
samples.evidence: Every command in api-keys.ts, cells.ts, docs.ts, files.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts, tabs.ts, sheets-import.ts, status.ts, ctx.ts and schema.ts repeats the same first line. A single narrowing in `getGlobalOpts` (with the overloaded `docs/slides/notes content|export` commands keeping their own vocabulary check, as they already do via InvalidFormatError) would make "validate before the side effect" structural instead of a convention every new command must remember. finding.summary: `sheets import` silently ignores `--start` for exported `ref,value,formula` CSVs, but the agent-facing schema still advertises it unconditionally
finding.evidence: `sheets-import.ts` now branches on `isCellTable(rows)` and calls `buildCellMapFromTable(rows)`, which imports by reference and never uses `parseStartRef(localOpts.start)`. The schema registry entry for `sheets.import` (registry.ts:556-562) still lists `'--start': { type: 'string', ..., description: 'Top-left cell', default: 'A1' }` with no note that it is inert for the header this repo's own `sheets export` writes, and `packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:348` likewise documents `--start <ref> | Top-left cell for import | A1` unqualified (the by-reference behaviour is only mentioned in the *export* section at line 392). `docs/design/cli.md` says the schema is the agent interface; round 8 of this PR treated exactly this class of gap (`--raw` missing from the registry) as blocking and added a flag-name parity test — which cannot catch a flag whose documented meaning no longer matches. Design-fit corollary: the round-trip is opted into explicitly on export (`--raw`) but switched implicitly on import via header sniffing, so a user-authored grid CSV whose first three columns happen to be named ref/value/formula changes import semantics and drops `--start` with no diagnostic.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element verified in the tree. sheets-import.ts:92-95 does branch on isCellTable() and route to buildCellMapFromTable(rows), which takes no start argument; csv-parse.ts:110-113's own comment states "`--start` does not apply". No warning or diagnostic is emitted on that path. registry.ts:561 still advertises '--start' as 'Top-left cell' with default 'A1' and no qualification, in contrast to the sibling '--raw' entry (registry.ts:576-582) which received a full explanatory description; docs/design/cli.md:22-26 and 962-963 establish the runtime schema as the self-describing agent interface. packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:348 documents `--start <ref> | Top-left cell for import | A1` unqualified, with the by-reference behaviour explained only in the export section (lines 387-394). The header sniff (csv-parse.ts:100-107) matches on just the first three columns named ref/value/formula, so a user-authored grid CSV can silently flip import semantics. This is an agent-facing contract/spec-conformance gap and an approach-fit asymmetry (explicit opt-in on export vs implicit sniffing on import), squarely in the design-fit lane. No guard, caller, or existing note refutes it.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The "finding" is not a claim about repository code at all — it is the verbatim error string thrown by the repo's own review harness when the reviewing agent's credential pool drains (scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637, poolExhaustedError), prefixed with the harness's "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict" wrapper. It names no file, no line, no acceptance criterion, no duplicated module, and no design-doc gap, so there is nothing to locate as a design-fit defect. Moreover, the behaviour the message describes is the repo's deliberate, tested terminal state for a fully retired pool: ask.test.mjs:295-308 asserts this exact message and its kind/retryable shape as the single canonical report for a drained pool, and ask.test.mjs:328-349 asserts that the last-retired slot must report the POOL rather than the slot's own error, with failover to healthy credentials verified at ask.test.mjs:285-293 and the walk-then-stop bound at :351-361. So no defect is present as described; the quoted text is a reviewer-runtime infrastructure failure, not a defect in the change under review.
